beatText.opening.assembly: 01 / THE QUESTION Between code and the bench. How do you connect a firmware decision to something you can actually observe? I wrote the firmware, scheduled the power states and built the bring-up fixture for Mosslink, an environmental sensor. Firmware is code that controls a physical device. ↓ Follow the work 01 / BENCH STUDY COMMAND FIRMWARE DECISION 02 / BENCH STUDY BOARD COLLEAGUE'S CIRCUITRY 03 / ACCESS FIXTURE ADA'S BRING-UP FIXTURE 04 / BENCH STUDY OBSERVE BENCH OBSERVATION ILLUSTRATIVE MODEL / NOT A WIRING PLAN
beatText.power.cycle: 02 / THE SCHEDULE Low power is a schedule. I scheduled the firmware's power states. This teaching loop separates a device's work into three states. 01 Sleep Wait between work. 02 Measure Take a reading. 03 Transmit Send a report. ↶ Then back to Sleep. Explanatory teaching loop, not Mosslink's actual firmware. No timings or current values are shown. My working documents include state tables, timing diagrams and bench checklists: ways to describe the work to check. AN EXPLANATORY TEACHING LOOP 01 SLEEP 02 MEASURE 03 TRANSMIT RETURN TO SLEEP Not Mosslink's actual firmware. No timings or current values shown.
beatText.middle.relationship: 03 / THE BENCH From a command to a check. Bring-up means checking a new board's basic operation. My fixture makes its response available to bench instruments. 01 Command 02 Board 03 Fixture 04 Observe Ada wrote the firmware and scheduled its power states. State tables and timing diagrams are part of her working documents; this is not a reproduction of that firmware. I wrote the firmware and built the fixture. A colleague designed the PCB and analogue front end. Command → board → fixture → observation. An explanatory relationship, not electrical wiring. 01 / BENCH STUDY COMMAND FIRMWARE DECISION 02 / BENCH STUDY BOARD COLLEAGUE'S CIRCUITRY 03 / ACCESS FIXTURE ADA'S BRING-UP FIXTURE 04 / BENCH STUDY OBSERVE BENCH OBSERVATION ILLUSTRATIVE MODEL / NOT A WIRING PLAN
beatText.proof.boundaries: 04 / THE EVIDENCE Two numbers. Different evidence. INPUTS TO AN ESTIMATE MEASURED Sleep and transmit current on the bench. + ASSUMED The reporting interval. → 2 years Projected battery life A SEPARATE OBSERVATION A continuous run on the bench. → 72 hours The longest observed run Authored explanation of the supplied fictional notes, not the original spreadsheet or a measured trace. The run does not establish two years of operation. An estimate is not two years of observed operation. INPUTS TO AN ESTIMATE Measured sleep / transmit current on the bench + assumed reporting interval 2 YEARS Projected battery life A SEPARATE OBSERVATION Continuous bench run Longest recorded duration 72 HOURS Observed Explanatory diagram from the fictional notes. Not the original spreadsheet or a measured trace.
beatText.close.evidence: 05 / THE SCOPE A connection. Not a leap. I connect firmware decisions to bench observations through power-state scheduling and the bring-up fixture, while keeping the evidence limits visible. Engineering samples assembled 40 Tested on the bench 6 Sent to customers 0 Six highlighted cells mark the bench-tested subset of forty. This illustrative count is not a pass/fail chart. One preliminary emissions check passed. Full qualification is unfinished.
